narrative_purpose: Anchors the cold open on the physical object the whole chapter interrogates: a cracked-open piece of crust whose fresh face shows the iron that had to be manufactured in a dying star.
subject: A dark rock broken cleanly in two, both halves held in one gloved hand. The freshly exposed inner faces are turned up toward the viewer - darker than the weathered outside, finer-grained, with a faint sheen and scattered pinpoint metallic glints across them. The outer surfaces are dulled and slightly reddened.
scene: Outdoors on a riverbank in dense forest at dusk. Wet dark pebbles and a shallow band of water behind the hand, out of focus. Faintly glowing low plants scattered along the bank edge give a soft cool light.
camera: Very close, looking almost straight down into the open palm, the broken faces filling most of the frame.
light: A single warm handheld lamp from upper left grazing across the broken faces to catch the metallic glints; cool cyan bounce from the glowing bank plants filling the shadows; the background falls into deep indigo.
palette: Deep teal-indigo stone, void-indigo shadows, a scarce warm amber raking light, tiny cool-white metallic glints, faint cyan from the plants.
style: Painterly naturalist field illustration, close-observed, textured brushwork.
detail_level: Very high on the broken faces - grain, sheen and glints legible; the surroundings soft and hazy.
composition: The hand and rock fill the lower two-thirds, angled from lower left to upper right. Open dark space at the upper left for a callout to sit cleanly.
consistency_notes: Same rock type as the cover: ordinary dark crust with iron in it, never glowing or crystalline. The glove is plain dark fabric with no insignia.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no logos, no insignia, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no glowing rock, no gemstones, no crystals
